newsitem.title: USA: Sears names new head of hardware, furniture units.
newsitem.headline: Sears names new head of hardware, furniture units.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. Thursday named William Salter, head of hard line goods at Sears' mall stores, to head the rapidly growing speciality chains, Sears Hardware stores and Homelife furniture stores.
As president of Sears' free-standing stores, Salter, 53, assumes the helm of an operation that is becoming a key driver of Sears' growth.

He succeeds Marvin Stern, 60, who is credited with helping Sears sharpen its ability to compete with electronic superstores. Stern will become an advisor to Sears, a step toward eventual retirement, the company said.
The retailer has opened 46 free-standing hardware stores so far this year and plans to launch another 29 before year-end. Sears hopes to have 500 hardware stores by 2000.
The newly opened hardware stores take about a year before they begin to turn a profit, but the older stores are solidly profitable, officials said.
Homelife furniture stores, however, have been a challenge. The chain will not make money this year but could in 1997.

"We are pleased that we will retain Marv Stern's extensive retail expertise, which has contributed greatly to the growth and success of the company," Sears Chairman Arthur Martinez said in a statement.

Stern began working at Sears in 1959 as a trainee in Chicago. He left Sears for several years in the 1980s to work for competitor Montgomery Ward but returned in 1988 and helped Sears take on consumer electronics giants like Best Buy Co. Sears' appliance departments were redesigned and renamed Brand Central and now carry more brand-name goods.
Stern was named head of Sears Hardware, Homelife and dealer-operated rural stores in 1995. Under his management, the formats have grown quickly, Martinez said.
"Stern has been talking about retirement for the last five years," said retail consultant Walter Loeb. "I'm delighted he's going to stay at Sears."
Also Thursday, Sears said Robert Mettler, who is president of apparel and home fashions at Sears' mall-based department stores, was named president of merchandising for Sears.
